module.purpose: Provides a React hook for subscribing to atom values with support for promise handling, delayed updates, and debugging in the Jotai state management library.
module.summary: This file implements the useAtomValue React hook which allows components to subscribe to atom values with automatic re-rendering when atoms change. It includes sophisticated promise handling for async atoms, a deprecated delay option, and debug value support. The hook uses a reducer to track value changes and effects to manage subscriptions, with special handling for promise-like values that can be continued after aborts.
module.businessContext: Enables React components to reactively access Jotai atom state. Critical for building reactive UIs where state changes must trigger component updates. Failure breaks reactivity and can cause stale UI.

detail.name: attachPromiseStatus
detail.signature: <T>(promise: PromiseLike<T> & { status?: 'pending' | 'fulfilled' | 'rejected'; value?: T; reason?: unknown }) => void

parameters.name: promise
parameters.type: PromiseLike<T> & { status?: 'pending' | 'fulfilled' | 'rejected'; value?: T; reason?: unknown }

preconditions: The input must be a PromiseLike (thenable) object.
The input object may have optional status, value, or reason properties that will be overwritten or populated.
postconditions: The input object's status property is set to 'pending', 'fulfilled', or 'rejected' as appropriate.
If the promise fulfills, the value property is set to the resolved value.
If the promise rejects, the reason property is set to the rejection reason.
The function returns void and does not modify the return type.
invariants: The function mutates the input object's status, value, and reason properties (if they exist).
The function attaches then handlers only if the status is not already set (truthy).
edgeCases: If the promise is already settled (status is 'fulfilled' or 'rejected'), the function still sets up handlers which will fire asynchronously (but status is already set, so the handlers may not run if the promise is already settled? Actually, the handlers are attached to the promise, so they will run immediately if the promise is already settled? The thenable's then method behavior is implementation-specific, but typically if the promise is already settled, the handler will be called asynchronously. The function does not check if the promise is already settled, it only checks the status property. If the promise is already settled but the status property is not set, the handlers will still be attached and will run, setting the status and value/reason.
If the promise is not thenable (doesn't have a then method), calling promise.then will throw. However, the type signature enforces PromiseLike, so this is a type error at compile time.
If the status property is already set (to a truthy value), the function does nothing (does not attach handlers).

errorPolicy.onInvalidInput: The function does not validate input beyond TypeScript types. If the input does not have a then method, a runtime error will occur when calling promise.then.

units.name: use

detail.name: use
detail.signature: React.use || (<T>(promise: PromiseLike<T> & { status?: 'pending' | 'fulfilled' | 'rejected'; value?: T; reason?: unknown }): T => { if (promise.status === 'pending') { throw promise } else if (promise.status === 'fulfilled') { return promise.value as T } else if (promise.status === 'rejected') { throw promise.reason } })
detail.returnType: typeof React.use | (<T>(promise: PromiseLike<T> & { status?: 'pending' | 'fulfilled' | 'rejected'; value?: T; reason?: unknown }) => T)
edgeCases: When promise.status is 'pending', the shim throws the promise object itself.
When promise.status is 'fulfilled', the shim returns promise.value.
When promise.status is 'rejected', the shim throws promise.reason.
When promise.status is undefined or any other value, the shim throws promise.reason (which may be undefined).
When React.use exists, the native implementation is used instead of the shim.
detail.summary: A compatibility shim for React.use that provides a synchronous hook-like interface for resolving continuables (Promise-like objects with optional status/value/reason properties). Falls back to a custom implementation when React.use is not available.

specLiterals.role: Defines the valid status values for the promise-like objects that the shim handles.

detail.name: continuablePromiseMap
invariants: Each promise object used as a key maps to its attached status callback or a resolved promise.
edgeCases: When a promise is not present in the map, `attachPromiseStatus` will attach a new status callback.
When a promise is already in the map and its value is a resolved promise, attaching a status callback is a no-op (the promise is already resolved).
stateMutations: Mutates the global `continuablePromiseMap` by adding entries when `attachPromiseStatus` is called with new promises.
detail.summary: A Map storing promise continuations (status callbacks) keyed by the promise object itself, used to track and update the status of promises within the continuable promise system.
